quiz.title: Module 2 — Tuesday — Speaking With Impact
quiz.description: Tuesday's quiz covers the flat delivery of a rookie communicator against the full vocal range of a natural one, recording yourself to build self-awareness, moving with purpose, frameworks such as PREP and STAR under pressure, matching face to voice, what keeps people stuck at pretty good, and the reading analogy.

questions.prompt: According to the video, what is one major characteristic of a rookie communicator's vocal delivery?
options: Using varied pitch and volume to emphasize important points.
Speaking with expressive emotions throughout a presentation.
Using pauses strategically to create impact.
Speaking with a flat delivery, using nearly the same speed, pitch, volume, and emotion throughout.
questions.explanation: The rookie delivery holds one setting: same speed, same pitch, same volume, same emotion. Nothing in the voice signals what matters.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of recording yourself answering an unexpected question and reviewing the transcript?
options: To memorize responses to common questions.
To develop self-awareness by identifying unclear explanations, repetition, rambling, and filler words.
To increase your speaking speed regardless of clarity.
To compare your vocabulary with that of professional speakers.
questions.explanation: The transcript shows what you actually said rather than what you meant to say. Repetition, rambling and filler are far easier to spot written down.

questions.prompt: What distinguishes a natural communicator from a pretty good communicator when it comes to using their voice?
options: A natural communicator uses only a low pitch to sound authoritative.
A natural communicator avoids emotional expression to maintain professionalism.
A natural communicator uses their full vocal range intentionally, adjusting different vocal elements to suit the message.
A natural communicator speaks loudly and quickly in every situation.
questions.explanation: The difference is range used on purpose. A pretty good speaker has a reliable delivery; a natural one reshapes it to fit the moment.

questions.prompt: According to the video, what is the main rule for using body movement effectively while communicating?
options: Move with purpose so your gestures support the message rather than distract from it.
Keep your hands completely still throughout every conversation.
Use the same gestures repeatedly to establish consistency.
Move continuously to prevent the audience from losing interest.
questions.explanation: Movement should carry meaning. Stillness and constant motion both cost something — what matters is whether the gesture backs up the words.

questions.prompt: Why are communication frameworks such as PREP, STAR, and the 3-2-1 method useful?
options: They eliminate the need to understand the topic being discussed.
They help speakers use more technical vocabulary in their responses.
They encourage speakers to explain every thought that comes to mind.
They help speakers organize their thoughts into clear, concise, and coherent responses, especially under pressure.
questions.explanation: A framework gives the answer a shape before you start speaking. That matters most when you are put on the spot and have no time to plan.

questions.prompt: According to the video, why is it important to synchronize facial expressions with vocal emotion?
options: Facial expressions are more important than the actual message in every situation.
When facial expressions and vocal delivery communicate matching emotions, the audience can better feel the intended meaning.
Matching facial expressions and vocal emotion prevents all communication misunderstandings.
Facial expressions should always be exaggerated to make a speaker memorable.
questions.explanation: Face and voice are read together. When they agree, the emotion lands; when the voice says one thing and the face another, the listener senses the conflict.

questions.prompt: What does the video identify as a major reason why people remain stuck at the level of pretty good communicators?
options: They lack the vocabulary required to discuss complex subjects.
They use too many communication frameworks in everyday conversations.
They fear being judged, which prevents them from exploring the full range of their vocal and expressive abilities.
They use too much body language when speaking.
questions.explanation: Playing it safe protects you from looking foolish, but it also caps your range. Getting past pretty good means risking a delivery you cannot fully control yet.

questions.prompt: In the video, the speaker explains the value of reading books using an analogy about building an army of soldiers. What does this analogy mean?
options: Each book provides knowledge and experience that can help you face challenges and make better decisions.
Reading books is useful only when preparing for competitive situations.
Successful people should read only books written by entrepreneurs.
Reading more books guarantees that you will never make mistakes.
questions.explanation: Each book adds a soldier to the ranks. You are not guaranteed to win, but the more you have read, the more you have to draw on when a problem arrives.
